description: 回合结束后的温和回望。目光先转向用户，身体随之前倾并微微侧转、头也转过去，轻点头一次，闭眼浅笑一拍后睁眼回正。覆盖头、视线、表情与上身倾斜；不表示任务成功，不收电脑、不移动腿、手保持原位。

reviewNotes.revision3: Revision 2 was limited to the face and head because reactions could only own those channels, which capped the head-region travel at 1.7px at 280px: the turn could not be seen. Reactions may now also own the silhouette levers (ParamBodyAngleX/Z, ParamShiftX, ParamHairFront/Back), so this revision leans the upper body toward the user as the eyes lead and the head follows.
reviewNotes.measuredLevers: Silhouette displacement at 280px: ParamShiftX 60 = 15.5px, ParamBodyAngleX 12 = 4.8px, ParamAngleZ 18 = 2.8px, ParamBodyAngleZ 8 = 2.4px, ParamHairBack 1 = 1.6px. ParamAngleX 30 = 0.3px and the arms = 0.2px, so head rotation and arm raise are detail, not silhouette.
reviewNotes.frameBudget: ParamShiftX 25 keeps ~31px of slack on the right edge and 40 keeps ~19px; 60 leaves 3px, so the lean stays at 25. The ground line does not move (bbox bottom is constant at 808 for every lean), so the grounding contract is unaffected. Verified with build/_zoom_review/measure_lean.py.
reviewNotes.neckLimit: Revision 3 tilted the head to ParamAngleZ 18. At rest the chin covers the neck entirely, so a tilt lifts the chin and exposes the underside of the flat face art, and this model has no neck layer for that (34 layers, no neck drawable). Neck fragmentation -- band rows whose visible skin is split into more than one run -- measures 3 at rest, 12 at tilt 18 and 3 at tilt 8. The body lean carries the motion, not the tilt (280px motion 26.56 at tilt 14 vs 26.26 at tilt 8), so revision 4 caps ParamAngleZ at 8 and raises ParamAngleX to 26 to keep the turn readable. Verified with build/_zoom_review/tilt_final.py.
reviewNotes.seamFix: Revision 4 still split the torso: the user saw the part above a line on the upper chest follow the head while the rest did not. Measured per-axis, the largest row-to-row step in the torso under ParamAngleZ 8 was 27.9px and it sat at y=356, high on the chest; ParamBodyAngleZ 5 scored 5.8px and ParamAngleX 26 scored 2.6px, both at the waist where a fold belongs. The side-tilt therefore moves to the body axis: revision 5 uses ParamAngleZ 3 and ParamBodyAngleZ 12, which puts the largest step back at the waist (19.9px at y=580, in the same range as the body's own 18.2px fold), cuts neck fragmentation from 6 to 2, and keeps the motion (280px 27.07 vs 26.63). Verified with build/_zoom_review/rebalance.py.
reviewNotes.bodyBudget: Revision 5 leaned at full amplitude. Per-axis isolation then showed the collar ruffle and the sleeves separate because the ruffle follows the torso while the arms keep their own anchors: the mismatch is driven by the body axes and ShiftX (+34px combined) and not by the head tilt, which contributes -3.2px. Motion is bought by those same body axes, so the value comes from that curve: at the real 280px size the mismatch is 0.8px at body scale 0, 7.0px at 0.5, 11.1px at 0.75 and 13.6px at 1.0, while motion saturates by 0.75 (24.76 of a reachable 27.82). Revision 6 therefore leans at 0.6: motion ~23 of 27 for roughly half the mismatch. Verified with build/_zoom_review/lean_tradeoff.py.
reviewNotes.noHeadTilt: Revisions 3-6 all drove ParamAngleZ. Measured from a clean zero base with the hem as anchor, that axis translates the whole upper body sideways instead of rotating the head in place: at 840px the shift is +9.5 at the hair, -20.1 at the neck, -24.5 at the chest, -18.2 at the apron and ~0 at the skirt, i.e. it flips sign at the waist. That is the split the user reports, and at the 280px desktop size it is -6.7px at the neck and -8.2px at the chest for a tilt of 8 degrees. ParamAngleZ also bought almost nothing: per-axis isolation put its contribution to the collar/sleeve mismatch at -3.2px. Revision 7 therefore sets it to zero and keeps the head turn on ParamAngleX (0.4px of outline movement) with the side lean on ParamBodyAngleZ. Verified with build/_zoom_review/z_block.py.
reviewNotes.bodyRemoved: Revisions 3-7 drove the body (ParamBodyAngleX/Z, ParamShiftX) to raise readability. The defect the user reports is a misalignment, and on the peak pose the figure's centre of mass moves +31.9px while the two arm windows move only +13.3px and +3.4px: the arms lag the body. Which deformer path leaves the arms behind could not be isolated from the exported rig data, so revision 8 removes the body motion from this action. A head/face-only reaction cannot misalign against itself. Kept: the head turn, the gaze lead, the nod, the eye-smile beat and the hair follow. The body-axis readability gain is deferred until the rig routing is understood.
reviewNotes.turnHalved: Revision 8 removed the body channels, but the preview still showed a misalignment. Measured on its key poses (clip rendered alone, no background layer), the torso and skirt do not move at all while the left arm window drifts up to +5.1px: armL-torso reaches +5.2px at a 26 degree turn. Since the body channels are zero, that residual tracks ParamAngleX, which drives the same upper-body warp the tilt did. Revision 9 therefore halves the turn to 13 degrees, expecting ~2.6px. If that is still visible the remaining lever is the rig, not the data.

keyframes.label: 结束当前工作，保持闭嘴
目光先转向用户，头与身体都还没跟上
倾到最大，视线仍落在用户身上
对着用户轻轻点头一次
点头回弹，笑眼开始合上
笑眼停留一拍，让表情被看懂
回正，交还原先的坐姿或站姿
